name: POSIX Shell Command Language
summary: The shell command language standardised by POSIX.2 (IEEE 1003.2-1992) and now in XCU Chapter 2 of POSIX.1/Single UNIX Specification; a codification of the Bourne shell plus KornShell features, implemented by dash, ash, yash, ksh, bash --posix and others.
standards: The Open Group Base Specifications Issue 8

level_notes.1: Normative text is XCU Chapter 2 (Shell Command Language) plus the sh, test, printf, read, getopts... utility pages and XBD chapters on regular expressions, environment variables and utility conventions; it is freely readable on pubs.opengroup.org (Issue 8 = POSIX.1-2024; Issue 7 2018 edition also linked). The informative rationale is XRAT C.2. The ISO version (ISO/IEC 9945) is paywalled. Austin Group bug reports serve as the proposal process.
level_notes.0: There is no reference implementation; dash (Debian/Ubuntu /bin/sh), BusyBox ash, FreeBSD sh (all Almquist-shell descendants), yash and Oils OSH aim at POSIX conformance. Smoosh is an executable formal semantics written in Lem; Morbig is a static POSIX shell parser. Oils' spec/ directory is a large cross-shell conformance suite.
level_notes.2: Most tutorials teach bash; the ones listed here are specifically about portable/POSIX sh.
